verdict.reasoning: Patient reports insect sting to the arm a few minutes ago and difficulty breathing: 'I got stung by a wasp... on my arm' and when asked if the sting occurred, 'it was, just a few minutes ago.' He also states 'I've, I'm kind of struggling to breathe at the moment.'

Rash and erythema with puncture at sting site are described: 'I've got a bit of a, a rash on my arm where I got stung,' and 'It's slightly red, yeah and kind of there's, a bit of a, like a hole there, where I think that the wasp, stung me.'

Patient reports right-sided lip soreness and abnormal tongue sensation: 'it's just kind of on the right-hand side... it's just a bit sore' and earlier 'there's a bit of swelling in my lips. My tongue feels a bit weird.'

He notes prior breathing difficulty but currently mild and is anxious about worsening: 'You've been having some difficulty breathing' / 'Yeah,' and later 'I don't feel like it's like particularly acute, but I'm just kind of a bit anxious that it might get a bit worse.'
No medications taken yet: 'have you... taken any antihistamines or anything like that?' / Patient: 'Not at the moment, no. Nothing, nothing yet.'
No history of anaphylaxis and no EpiPen: 'Have you got history of anaphylaxis?' / 'Uh, not that I know of.' and 'Have you ever been given an EpiPen?' / 'Uh, I haven't no.'

History of eczema and intermittent anxiety/panic without meds: 'I've had eczema before... that's kind of the major thing' and 'Do you suffer from anxiety or panic attacks?' / 'yeah, sometimes, occasionally.' / 'Have you ever been on medication for that?' / 'no.'

Penicillin allergy and denial of pet/food allergies: 'I'm allergic to penicillin.' and 'do you have allergies to any kind of, cats, or dogs, or pets?' / 'not that I know of' and 'you've got no food allergies as far as you're aware?' / 'No.'

Denies family history of acute reactions: 'in your family, is there any history of any illnesses, or, any history of any kind of acute reactions?' / 'not that I think is particularly relevant, no. I don't have, I don't have any.'
Occupation, living situation, and pet are described: 'What do you work as?' / 'I am a... computer scientist.' 'you living alone?' / 'Yes.' 'Do you have any pets at home?' / 'I have a cat, at home.'

Doctor assesses localized allergic reaction to likely bee/wasp, non-anaphylactic and stable: 'one of the two' (bee or wasp), 'it seems to me like this is a localised allergic reaction,' and 'I don't feel that you're having a life-threatening... allergic reaction.'

Anxiety related to sting is discussed, consistent with health anxiety: patient says he's 'feeling like slightly anxious' and 'just kind of a bit anxious that it might get a bit worse,' and doctor notes 'I can understand it, it is quite anxiety provoking.'
Penicillin allergy is confirmed: 'I'm allergic to penicillin.'

Doctor recommends chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg up to 6 times per day or a once-daily antihistamine: 'you can get Piriton or Chlorphenamine, and you can take one tablet, four milligrams, up to about six times a day... Or you can just take a one-a-day one, whichever is your preference.'

Urgent care advice for airway symptoms and deterioration: doctor warns about 'swelling of the lips, difficulty breathing... something called stridor' and says, 'if anything changes, if anything deteriorates... go straight to A and E... if it's progressing rapidly, it's better to go straight to A and E.'

Monitoring sting site and potential antibiotics for spreading redness/infection: 'if the redness in your arm spreads, and it feels hot, or you have signs of any localised infection. We may need to think about other treatments, like an antibiotic.'

Education on anaphylaxis, red flags, and low threshold to recontact: 'I'm gonna leave a link to some information about anaphylactic reactions... just for you to be aware what symptoms are. If those kind of things happen, get back to us. If you're feeling worried, just have a lower threshold for having a chat with us.'

'No EpiPen or allergy testing indicated now' and possible workup if recurrent: 'on the basis of what you've told me, I don't think you need any allergy testing. I think this is just a straightforward localised reaction' and 'if... you're having these kind of reactions on a regular basis... We might need to think about blood testing.' No EpiPen was given or recommended.

Doctor comments on normal breathing and speech, no stridor: 'Your breathing seems all right to me right now' and demonstrates stridor as something he does not hear: 'Thankfully, you don't have anything like that right now.' Patient is conversing in full sentences throughout.
Doctor notes no visible lip swelling: 'your, your lips don't seem swollen to me right now' and later, 'you mentioned swelling of your lip. Thankfully I can't see any of that right now.'

Arm findings: slight erythema, blotchy rash, puncture, no swelling: 'That looks OK to me right now... does it look red to you at the moment?' / 'It's slightly red... there's... a hole there, where... the wasp stung me.' Doctor asks about swelling, and patient replies, 'Not particularly... a bit of a rash. It doesn't feel like, particularly swollen.'
